questions.stem: A seventeen-year-old starts an Arkansas mobile notary business and buys a bond. Which qualification is missing?
questions.explanation: Arkansas applicants must be at least eighteen.
feedback: Correct. Purchasing a bond does not change age eligibility.
Home ownership is not required.
No college requirement is listed.
County employment is not required.

questions.stem: A Tennessee resident commutes to an Arkansas office. Which address information establishes the nonresident connection?
options: Residential address and Arkansas employer's street address
questions.explanation: The application requires the adjoining-state residence and Arkansas employment address.
feedback: A mailbox does not establish the stated employment connection.
Correct. Provide both actual addresses.
An email omits the required street addresses.
A relative's address does not describe the applicant's connection.

questions.stem: A permanent resident seeks an Arkansas commission and assumes only citizens qualify. What does the handbook provide?
options: Permanent residents need a law license
questions.explanation: The listed status requirement permits United States citizens or permanent resident aliens.
feedback: The list also permits permanent residents.
A law license is not this status condition.
Correct. The remaining qualifications still apply.
Temporary presence does not establish listed status.

questions.stem: An Arkansas applicant cannot read English but offers to have a colleague complete every notarial certificate. Which result follows?
options: English is needed only for RON
The applicant must satisfy the English literacy requirement
questions.explanation: Applicants must be able to read and write English.
feedback: Another person's skill cannot replace the applicant's qualification.
Bond value does not establish literacy.
The requirement applies to ordinary applicants.
Correct. The applicant must personally meet it.

questions.stem: An applicant had a notary commission revoked six years ago. Which Arkansas eligibility issue requires attention?
options: The color of the old seal
questions.explanation: The handbook requires no prior commission revocation during the past ten years.
feedback: Correct. Six years falls inside that period.
The published period is ten years.
An employer cannot waive the qualification.
Seal color does not resolve the revocation history.

questions.stem: A new applicant lists Jane Marie Bell on the bond but Jane Bell in the online signature. What should be corrected?
options: The name must match across the application and bond
questions.explanation: The name and signature must match the bond and application requirements.
feedback: Browser settings do not cure inconsistent names.
Correct. Make the names consistent before filing.
A delivery address cannot fix the name inconsistency.
Matching only the surname is insufficient.

questions.stem: An Arkansas resident lives in Saline County and works in Pulaski County. What establishes the commission county?
options: The county with the lowest recording fee
questions.explanation: An Arkansas resident's commission county is the home county.
feedback: A customer's location does not determine commissioning.
Employment does not replace this resident rule.
Correct. Saline County supplies the resident commission county.
Filing price does not determine county eligibility.

questions.stem: A nonresident military spouse employed in Arkansas seeks the special eligibility route. Which action follows the official entry page?
options: Contact the Secretary of State about the military-spouse route
questions.explanation: The official page directs qualifying nonresident military spouses to contact the office.
feedback: An inaccurate residence is not a qualification method.
The special route does not eliminate application requirements.
Software does not establish ordinary eligibility.
Correct. Obtain the office's route-specific instructions.

questions.stem: A surety contract comes from an Arkansas business that has never satisfied the Insurance Department registration requirements. What is the issue?
options: The provider must qualify under the stated bond rules
Every local business can issue it
The applicant can replace registration with a receipt
questions.explanation: The permitted Arkansas-business surety contract depends on the stated registration and compliance conditions.
feedback: Correct. Confirm the proposed surety qualifies.
Incorporation alone is insufficient.
A receipt cannot establish the required registration.
The provider's legal qualification is substantive.

questions.stem: An Arkansas applicant has learned general notary practices in another state and skips Arkansas law. What must the applicant still do?
options: Rely entirely on the other state's handbook
Review Arkansas law and understand Arkansas notary duties
Ask customers to supply all rules
questions.explanation: Arkansas's qualification declaration includes reviewing its notary law and understanding the duties.
feedback: Another state's rules cannot replace state-specific review.
Correct. Apply Arkansas's own law.
Customers do not supply the applicant's legal qualification.
Supply advertising is not the required law review.

questions.stem: A new applicant passes the Arkansas exam but uploads only the bond. Which document is still required?
questions.explanation: The current portal guide requires a certificate of Arkansas notary exam completion.
feedback: An evaluation is not the missing prescribed certificate.
A wedding license is unrelated to ordinary qualification.
Correct. Upload the exam evidence.
A website review does not prove examination completion.

questions.stem: An applicant finds a 2023 portal login and cannot use the current account system. What does the current guide instruct?
options: Create an account in the current portal
questions.explanation: Accounts predating January 25, 2024 require a new current-system account.
feedback: Customers should not receive account credentials.
Another person's account does not identify the applicant.
The web-filed process uses a portal account.
Correct. Follow the current account setup instructions.

questions.stem: A bond shows a commission start date, and the current Arkansas form asks for that date. What does the portal guide say?
options: Use the bond's commission start date in the ordinary case
Always use the business incorporation date
Leave it blank despite a required field
questions.explanation: The guide ordinarily directs use of the bond's stated commission start date.
feedback: Correct. Contact the office if the date is uncertain.
Birth date serves a different purpose.
Business incorporation does not set the commission date.
Required information must be completed.

questions.stem: A web-filed application has an incomplete required field highlighted in red. What is the appropriate next step?
options: Ignore it because the exam was passed
questions.explanation: The portal identifies incomplete or erroneous fields for correction.
feedback: Another payment does not complete missing data.
Correct. Resolve the field error.
A second identity does not correct the application.
Passing the exam does not fill required fields.

questions.stem: An applicant's upload fails after the portal sat idle. What troubleshooting check does the guide identify?
options: Whether a customer approved the upload
Whether the applicant is still logged in
Whether a different state issued the bond
questions.explanation: The portal guide notes that inactivity can end the login session.
feedback: Stamp shape does not restore a timed-out session.
Customer consent is not portal authentication.
Correct. Check the session before retrying.
An unrelated state's bond is not the session issue.

questions.stem: After selecting Checkout, an applicant sees Processing and wants to close the browser. What does the current Arkansas guide direct?
questions.explanation: Leaving while processing can interrupt payment and the filing.
feedback: Closing may interrupt the transaction.
Repeated Back actions may interrupt processing.
Duplicate attempts are not the stated instruction.
Correct. Allow the current payment to finish.

questions.stem: An Arkansas applicant elects ACH payment. What additional action completes payment authorization?
options: Take the exam a second time
Ask the county to debit the account
questions.explanation: ACH processing requires accepting the displayed authorization.
feedback: Correct. Follow the guide's authorization step.
A seal is not payment authorization.
Retesting does not authorize an ACH debit.
The state portal presents its own agreement.

questions.stem: A saved card in the Arkansas portal contains an error. What payment-wallet action is described?
options: Edit any saved field in place
Add a new method or delete the saved method
Share the card with another applicant
Use the exam certificate as payment
questions.explanation: The guide says saved methods cannot be edited, and may be added or deleted.
feedback: The guide says saved methods are not editable.
Correct. Replace the erroneous saved method through those controls.
Sharing payment details is not the described repair.
Exam evidence is not a payment method.

questions.stem: A web-filed Arkansas application is awaiting review. Where does the guide tell the applicant to track it?
questions.explanation: The portal work queue displays the filing status.
feedback: The applicant's state filing is not tracked in a customer journal.
Election results do not show notary application status.
Correct. Use the official work queue.
A vendor advertisement is not the filing record.

questions.stem: An approval produces oath certificates bearing a misspelled name. What should the applicant do?
options: Correct it with whiteout after recording
Ask a customer to choose a new name
Contact the Secretary of State promptly
questions.explanation: The handbook instructs applicants to report incorrect certificate information immediately.
feedback: The commission record needs correction.
Altering issued documents is not the stated correction process.
The customer's preference does not correct the state record.
Correct. Resolve the official certificate discrepancy.

questions.stem: An appointee has two oath certificates and asks why both go to the county recorder with the bond. What happens there?
options: The clerk administers the oath and signs the certificates
The clerk retakes the examination for the applicant
questions.explanation: County recording includes the applicant's oath before the clerk and the clerk's signatures.
feedback: Correct. Follow the county recording stage.
Software sales do not complete the oath.
State return remains required.
The applicant must personally qualify.

questions.stem: A county offers to forward an Arkansas applicant's recorded oath to the state. Who remains responsible for ensuring it is filed?
questions.explanation: The handbook keeps responsibility for timely state filing with the applicant.
feedback: A vendor does not oversee the oath filing.
Correct. Confirm the state has processed it.
Insurance does not transfer the applicant's responsibility.
A recipient is not responsible for commissioning.

questions.stem: An appointee wants to upload the recorded oath using the July 2026 portal. Which method does that guide permit?
options: A photograph sent to a customer
Mail or in-person delivery to the state
Ordinary portal upload of the oath
questions.explanation: The guide says recorded oaths cannot currently be submitted online.
feedback: A social message is not the prescribed filing method.
A customer photo is not state filing.
Correct. Use the physical return instructions.
The guide expressly excludes online oath submission.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary pays for renewal three months before expiration and expects the listed portal renewal route. What window does the July 2026 guide identify?
options: Any time in the ten-year term
Only after an entire year of expiration
Expired or within sixty days before expiration
questions.explanation: The guide permits renewal when the commission is expired or within sixty days of expiry.
feedback: The described route has a defined window.
The guide does not require waiting one year.
It permits a broader pre-expiration interval.
Correct. Follow the current guide's eligibility window.

questions.stem: A notary's old Arkansas commission has expired, and the July 2026 guide lists expired records as renewable. What should the notary use for current filing instructions?
options: An older FAQ's conflicting post-expiration limit without checking
questions.explanation: The newest dated official portal guide expressly includes expired commissions.
feedback: Correct. Its instructions address the current portal route.
The older conflict is documented and should not silently replace the new guide.
A customer's assurance is not an official process source.
A vendor's policy does not govern state filing.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary seeks renewal but offers the bond covering the ending commission. What evidence does the handbook require?
options: Only proof that the old premium was paid
A new surety bond with the renewal
questions.explanation: Renewal requires a new bond and the application requirements.
feedback: The old premium is not the new bond.
Correct. Secure the renewal bond.
A promise cannot replace the required bond.
Employer support is not a surety instrument.

questions.stem: A notary changes a residential address inside the same Arkansas county. Which filing route is described?
options: A request to the seal vendor only
questions.explanation: The handbook allows the same-county address amendment through the online portal.
feedback: Notary address updates are state matters.
Address changes must be reported within thirty days.
Correct. Update the official state record.
A vendor update does not amend the state record.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary changes a legal name after marriage and has an ordinary photocopy of the license. What does the name-change process require?
options: Only an online profile name edit
The paper amendment and certified name-change documentation
questions.explanation: Name changes require a paper filing with certified supporting documentation.
feedback: An email alias does not document the legal change.
The current guide excludes online name changes.
Customer permission cannot amend a commission.
Correct. A plain photocopy is insufficient.

questions.stem: A notary moves from one Arkansas county to another. What commission action does the handbook describe?
options: Transfer through the circuit clerk and obtain a seal reflecting the new county
Automatically become a notary of every state
Wait until the old stamp wears out
questions.explanation: A county move requires commission transfer and a new county-correct seal.
feedback: Correct. Follow the official transfer instructions.
The record and seal must reflect the required county.
An Arkansas move does not create interstate authority.
Equipment wear does not set the reporting obligation.

questions.stem: An adjoining-state resident's Arkansas employment moves to another county. What must be updated?
options: The commission's county/employment information through the transfer process
Nothing because residence is outside Arkansas
questions.explanation: The out-of-state notary's Arkansas employment location supports the commission record.
feedback: The customer's address does not update the notary's record.
Correct. Follow the nonresident transfer instructions.
Payroll does not amend the official commission.
Nonresident status does not eliminate employment-related updates.
questions.reference: p. 7, Notaries who live out of state

questions.stem: A nonresident commissioned through Arkansas employment ends that employment and has no remaining qualifying connection. What limits the commission?
options: The commission depends on maintaining the Arkansas employment connection
questions.explanation: The handbook says the employment-based nonresident commission remains valid only while the required Arkansas employment continues.
feedback: Advertising cannot preserve eligibility.
Ink supply is unrelated to eligibility.
Correct. The qualifying connection must continue.
A printed date does not replace ongoing eligibility.
questions.reference: p. 7, Arkansas notaries who live out of state

questions.stem: A notary discovers that the commission information filed with Arkansas has changed. What general reporting period does the handbook give for name or address changes?
questions.explanation: The handbook requires the amendment within thirty days of the change.
feedback: One year exceeds the stated period.
A future customer visit does not set the deadline.
Waiting for renewal misses the reporting requirement.
Correct. Use the route appropriate to the change.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary is commissioned in Washington County and asked to act in Benton County. What territorial rule applies?
options: A separate bond is required for each act county
Authority ends at the home county line
Only the Secretary of State may act outside Washington County
questions.explanation: Arkansas notarial jurisdiction is statewide during the commission.
feedback: Correct. Use the actual act county in the venue.
The handbook does not require a separate county-act bond.
County of commission does not limit state territory.
Ordinary commissioned notaries have statewide authority.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary visits a Mississippi client's office and is asked to use the Arkansas seal there. What should the notary do?
options: Proceed because the client is from Arkansas
Decline to act there under Arkansas authority
Use the Arkansas county as a fictional venue
Charge no fee to extend jurisdiction
questions.explanation: The Arkansas commission does not authorize acts performed in another state.
feedback: The client's origin does not extend territorial authority.
Correct. Arkansas authority operates within Arkansas.
A false venue cannot create jurisdiction.
A waived fee cannot extend the commission's territory.

questions.stem: An employer that paid an Arkansas employee's commission demands that the employee surrender the commission on resignation. Who holds the commission?
questions.explanation: The commission is issued to the individual, and the employer cannot revoke it.
feedback: Payment does not transfer the public office.
A salesperson does not hold the commission.
Correct. The notary retains responsibility for the commission and supplies.
A customer does not own the commission.

questions.stem: A Fayetteville signer brings a membership card with no photograph. The notary remains unsure of identity. What is appropriate?
options: Use the document title as proof
questions.explanation: The Arkansas notary must be satisfied that the person has the claimed identity.
feedback: A card does not automatically resolve identity.
Correct. Resolve the uncertainty before acting.
Payment does not identify the signer.
A title does not identify the person.

questions.stem: A long-standing neighbor appears to sign in Little Rock. The notary genuinely recognizes the neighbor. What does the handbook allow?
options: Only a newly issued passport is ever permitted
A neighbor never needs to appear
The neighbor may identify absent relatives
questions.explanation: The handbook's photo-ID recommendation recognizes personal recognition of the signer.
feedback: Correct. The notary must still be certain of identity.
The handbook does not impose that exclusive credential.
Personal knowledge does not waive appearance.
Recognition of one person cannot identify absent signers.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary advertises an exclusive list of legally mandatory ID cards copied from another state. What should guide actual decisions?
options: The customer's preferred number of cards
questions.explanation: Arkansas's handbook does not specify an exclusive acceptable-ID list for ordinary acts.
feedback: Another state's statutory list is not Arkansas's rule.
Card quantity alone does not resolve identity.
Correct. Apply the state's identity standard and recommended evidence.
Purchase price does not establish identity.

questions.stem: A signer shows an Arkansas driver's license but the photograph appears to depict someone else. Which action addresses the problem?
options: Ignore the mismatch because the license is governmental
Ask only whether the fee is accepted
Resolve the identity discrepancy before acting
questions.explanation: A recommended credential must still satisfactorily identify the person presenting it.
feedback: Government issuance does not erase a mismatch.
Copying a number does not establish identity.
A fee agreement does not resolve identity.
Correct. The notary must be satisfied about the actual person.

questions.stem: A company's courier delivers an employee's signed affidavit while the employee stays elsewhere. What is missing for an ordinary Arkansas notarization?
questions.explanation: The person whose signature is notarized must appear for the act.
feedback: Correct. A courier cannot supply the employee's appearance.
A logo cannot supply appearance.
Two couriers still do not produce the signer.
An invoice is unrelated to personal appearance.

questions.stem: A customer proposes an ordinary phone call to confirm an absent signer. The notary has no electronic commission or approved RON setup. What is appropriate?
options: Proceed if the voice sounds familiar
Ask the caller to text a seal image
Let the employer impersonate the signer
questions.explanation: Without the approved RON route, physical presence remains required.
feedback: A familiar voice does not satisfy ordinary appearance.
Correct. Arrange the lawful appearance method.
A seal image does not create remote authority.
An employer cannot substitute for the signer.

questions.stem: An Arkansas signer appears unable to understand what the document is. What should the notary assess before proceeding?
options: Whether the document uses expensive paper
Whether the fee can be increased
The signer's understanding of the document's nature
questions.explanation: The handbook instructs the notary to check that the signer understands the document's nature.
feedback: Paper quality does not establish understanding.
A higher fee cannot cure lack of understanding.
Correct. Resolve this prerequisite before acting.
Urgency does not replace the assessment.

questions.stem: A companion answers every question and the Arkansas signer quietly says the signature is unwanted. What should control?
questions.explanation: The handbook requires attention to whether the signer acts of their own free will.
feedback: A deadline cannot cure coercion.
An employer cannot supply the signer's willingness.
Payment does not establish consent.
Correct. Do not proceed while free will is unresolved.

questions.stem: A Little Rock notary and signer have no shared language and cannot communicate directly. What is the relevant handbook requirement?
options: Direct communication in a language both understand
A companion's assurance that all is well
questions.explanation: The handbook requires direct communication between notary and signer in a shared language.
feedback: Correct. Meet that requirement before acting.
A title cannot establish communication.
A business card does not supply mutual understanding.
An assurance does not replace the stated direct communication.

questions.stem: An Arkansas signer uses characters the notary does not understand for the signature. Which handbook checkpoint is implicated?
options: Use of letters or characters understood by signer and notary
questions.explanation: The handbook lists mutual understanding of the signature's letters or characters among pre-act checks.
feedback: This is a notarial procedure issue.
Correct. Resolve the checkpoint before completing the act.
Stamp purchasing does not address the signature.
Advertising expenditure is unrelated.

questions.stem: An Arkansas affidavit signer offers a signature but refuses to swear or affirm the statements. What is incomplete?
questions.explanation: An affidavit is a sworn written statement, requiring the affiant's oath or affirmation.
feedback: A receipt does not supply the sworn declaration.
A fee agreement does not supply an oath.
Correct. Signing alone does not complete the requested sworn act.
A mailing address does not substitute for the declaration.

questions.stem: A witness asks an Arkansas notary to administer a promise that forthcoming testimony will be truthful. Which function fits?
options: Administration of an oath or affirmation
questions.explanation: An oath may concern the truthfulness of testimony the witness will give.
feedback: Copy certification concerns reproduction of a record.
Renewal concerns the notary's appointment.
Seal registration does not administer testimony promises.
Correct. Use the appropriate oath or affirmation procedure.

questions.stem: A new corporate officer asks an Arkansas notary to administer an oath of faithful performance. Is that among the handbook's oath examples?
options: Yes, faithful performance of corporate duties is included
Only an Arkansas judge can administer any oath
Only court testimony may be sworn
Only birth records may be sworn
questions.explanation: The handbook includes faithful performance of corporate office among oath purposes.
feedback: Correct. Screen identity and other requirements.
The handbook authorizes notarial oaths.
Oaths are not confined to court testimony.
Birth records do not define the oath power.

questions.stem: Two borrowers attend an Arkansas signing at different times. The first certificate names both as appearing together. What should change?
options: Use the same false joint appearance statement
Use separate certificates matching each appearance
Have the first borrower sign for the second
questions.explanation: The handbook requires separate certificates when the signers cannot appear together.
feedback: The certificate must accurately describe appearance.
Correct. Each certificate follows its actual signer and appearance.
One borrower cannot supply another's personal appearance.
Removing dates makes the record inaccurate.

questions.stem: An Arkansas certificate says a signer appeared Monday, but the actual act takes place Tuesday. Which date belongs in the certificate?
questions.explanation: The certificate must state the actual date of the act.
feedback: Drafting does not determine the notarial date.
Mailing does not determine when the act happened.
Correct. Record the true act date.
Bond purchase relates to commissioning.

questions.stem: A notary commissioned in Garland County performs an act in Hot Spring County. Which county belongs in the certificate's venue?
options: Garland because it is on the seal
Hot Spring, where the act occurs
questions.explanation: Certificate venue identifies the actual location of the act.
feedback: Commission county and act venue can differ.
Residence does not determine this act's venue.
Venue must describe the real location.
Correct. Keep the seal's commission county accurate separately.

questions.stem: A client asks an Arkansas notary to sign an otherwise blank certificate so the client can fill it in later. What should the notary do?
options: Complete the certificate before signing and sealing
Sign now if payment is prepaid
questions.explanation: The notary must finish the certificate information before applying signature and seal.
feedback: Correct. This prevents later false insertions.
A required blank still leaves it incomplete.
Prepayment does not authorize a blank certificate.
The notary bears responsibility for certificate completion.

questions.stem: An Arkansas loan packet has only the notary's signature line and a space for a stamp. What is still needed?
options: A certificate describing the notarial act
questions.explanation: A signature and seal alone do not describe the required notarial act.
feedback: A logo does not state what occurred.
Correct. Include the proper completed certificate.
Bank-routing information does not certify the act.
A larger signature does not replace certificate wording.

questions.stem: An Arkansas certificate names a second person who never appeared. What does including that name represent?
options: A claim of appearance that the notary cannot truthfully make
An automatic appointment of the absent person
questions.explanation: The handbook says naming a signer verifies that person's appearance before the notary.
feedback: Preference cannot justify a false appearance statement.
A named signer conveys more than pagination.
Correct. Certify only what actually occurred.
A certificate does not appoint the signer.

questions.stem: A signer asks the Arkansas notary to certify an act that the notary believes did not occur. Which certificate principle controls?
options: Information must not be known or believed false
questions.explanation: A certificate is incomplete or defective when it contains information the notary knows or believes false.
feedback: Indemnity does not make a false statement true.
Employer approval cannot authorize false certification.
A deadline does not change the facts.
Correct. Do not make the requested false certification.

questions.stem: An Arkansas client can make an X but cannot write a conventional signature. What witness arrangement does the handbook describe for the mark?
options: At least one disinterested witness with the notary present
The notary acting alone as the client
questions.explanation: The mark procedure requires the mark before the notary and at least one disinterested witness.
feedback: Correct. Add the prescribed explanatory wording.
The handbook includes a witness requirement.
The witness must be disinterested.
The notary does not become the signer.

questions.stem: A signer makes a mark before an Arkansas notary and a proper witness. What additional certificate detail is described?
options: A promise that the mark resembles handwriting
A notation identifying the signer by mark and the witness
questions.explanation: The notary writes the prescribed mark-affixation notation identifying the participants.
feedback: Handwriting resemblance is not the required notation.
Correct. Record who made the mark and witnessed it.
Bank balances are unrelated.
A second commission number is not required.

questions.stem: An Arkansas principal cannot sign or make a mark and directs a disinterested third party to sign. How many disinterested witnesses are required?
questions.explanation: The alternative-signature procedure requires two disinterested witnesses and the notary.
feedback: The procedure requires witnesses.
One applies to the separate mark procedure.
Correct. Each signs beside the signature.
Five is not the described minimum.

questions.stem: A third party signs for an Arkansas principal who cannot sign or make a mark. What must the witnesses do?
options: Sign their names beside that signature before the notary
questions.explanation: The described procedure requires each disinterested witness's signature beside the principal's substituted signature.
feedback: Leaving prevents completion of the witness procedure.
Fee approval is not the witness duty.
Witnesses do not use the notary's seal.
Correct. Follow the complete statutory procedure.

questions.stem: A family member volunteers to sign for an Arkansas principal who cannot sign, but the principal gives no direction. What is missing?
options: The principal's direction to the disinterested third party
A translation of the office sign
questions.explanation: The substituted-signature procedure depends on the principal directing the signer in the required presence.
feedback: Correct. The third party cannot independently supply the principal's decision.
A business card does not establish direction.
Office signage is unrelated.
Parking validation does not establish authorization.

questions.stem: A notary is asked to take an Arkansas deposition but is not a certified court reporter. What does the handbook advise?
options: Accept because all notarizations are depositions
Do not accept depositions as an act of that notarial office
Replace the reporter with a seal
questions.explanation: The handbook warns that Arkansas court depositions require attestation by a certified court reporter.
feedback: A deposition has additional court requirements.
Correct. Follow the certified-reporter requirement.
A nickname does not satisfy deposition requirements.
A seal does not create reporter certification.

questions.stem: An Arkansas document has a signature by mark with a disinterested witness, but the mark was made outside the notary's presence. What remains unsatisfied?
options: The mark's required presence before the notary
The signer's choice of ink brand
questions.explanation: The handbook requires the mark to be affixed in the notary's presence.
feedback: Paper weight does not establish appearance.
Stamp cost is unrelated.
Correct. The prescribed procedure requires that presence.
The ink brand does not cure the missing presence.

questions.stem: A notary names every signer in a certificate because all names appear on the document, although only one attended. What is the proper scope?
options: Certify all signatures because the form lists them
Use the first signer to vouch for everyone
Certify only the actual appearance and act performed
questions.explanation: The Arkansas certificate must accurately identify who appeared and what happened.
feedback: A form's names cannot supply absent appearances.
Authorship is not the scope of this act.
One signer cannot replace every other appearance.
Correct. Use separate accurate certificates as needed.

questions.stem: An Arkansas traditional notary's employer announces that a journal is legally mandatory for every paper act. Which statement matches the handbook?
options: The handbook recommends a journal for traditional acts
The handbook forbids all paper journals
Every entry must be filed daily
Only electronic providers can record acts
questions.explanation: The handbook recommends a traditional register without describing it as generally compulsory.
feedback: Correct. Preserve the distinction between recommendation and duty.
The handbook encourages recordkeeping.
Daily filing is not the stated recommendation.
The notary may keep a register.

questions.stem: A subpoena concerns an Arkansas act performed years ago. Which journal purpose does the handbook identify?
questions.explanation: A register can help the notary reconstruct an act when called to testify.
feedback: A journal does not replace appointment.
Correct. Contemporaneous details can support recollection.
A journal does not guarantee the document's factual contents.
Records do not transfer notarial authority.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary says personal official records can never be evidence in court. What does the handbook state?
options: Only fee receipts can be evidence
Only electronic recordings can be evidence
Notary records and official papers are admissible in Arkansas courts
questions.explanation: The handbook describes notary records and official papers as admissible evidence.
feedback: The statement extends beyond receipts.
It is not limited to electronic recordings.
Correct. Maintain accurate records.
Admissibility does not turn an entry into a judgment.

questions.stem: An Arkansas journal records a loan signing but omits the date. Which suggested field would help distinguish it from later acts?
options: The date of the notarial act
questions.explanation: The suggested register format includes the act date.
feedback: A slogan does not identify the act's timing.
Carpet color is unrelated to the suggested field.
Vacation plans do not document the act.
Correct. Record the actual act date.

questions.stem: A register says only 'notarized' for an Arkansas appointment involving an oath. Which suggested detail would improve it?
options: The type of notarial act performed
questions.explanation: The suggested register identifies the act type.
feedback: Correct. Specify the actual oath or other act.
A card brand does not identify the notarial procedure.
Favorite color is irrelevant.
Commuting distance does not state the act.

questions.stem: Several Arkansas appointments involve the same customer but different records. What suggested register field distinguishes the records?
questions.explanation: The handbook suggests identifying the document type.
feedback: A birthstone does not describe the record.
Correct. Describe the actual document involved.
The bond logo is unrelated to these records.
Printer hardware does not identify the notarial record.

questions.stem: An Arkansas journal lists two signers only as 'the borrowers.' Which suggested information should be entered for each?
questions.explanation: The suggested format includes each notarized signer's name and address.
feedback: A combined nickname obscures individual identity.
The employer is not a substitute for each signer.
Correct. Identify the actual individuals.
The recipient's fax does not identify the signers.

questions.stem: A notary designing an Arkansas paper register wants one suggested field that connects the signer personally to the entry. Which is listed?
options: A copy of every bank statement
A signature by the seal vendor
questions.explanation: The handbook's suggested format includes the signer's signature.
feedback: The handbook does not suggest collecting every bank statement.
A vendor did not participate as the signer.
Medical history is not a suggested register field.
Correct. It identifies the actual participant's entry.

Use the required blue or black inking so the seal reproduces
Ask the client to imagine the impression

questions.stem: A supplier offers an Arkansas notary seal containing the Great Seal of the State. What is the correct response?

Remove the prohibited state Great Seal

questions.stem: A notary supervises copying a permitted private record in Arkansas, but the client requests wording saying its statements are legally correct. What wording matches the performed act?
options: A guarantee that every statement is enforceable
A legal opinion about every clause
An assurance that no dispute can arise
A true-copy statement limited to the reproduction
questions.explanation: Copy certification concerns reproducing the original rather than adjudicating its contents.
feedback: Enforceability is not established by copying.
A legal opinion is outside this copy certificate.
A notarial copy cannot prevent disputes.
Correct. Certify only the comparison actually performed.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary is named as a buyer in the agreement presented for notarization. What should the notary do?
options: Use another eligible notary because the notary is a party
Ask the seller to hold the seal
questions.explanation: A notary may not notarize a document to which the notary is a party.
feedback: A discount does not cure party status.
Correct. The transaction requires an impartial officer.
Concealing the name does not remove the interest.
Another person holding the seal does not cure the conflict.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary expects a personal financial gain from the transaction beyond the notarial service. Which rule applies?
options: Direct or indirect financial benefit creates a conflict
A larger stamp removes the benefit
Every signed waiver eliminates the conflict
Only cash received on the same day matters
questions.explanation: The handbook prohibits notarization of a document from which the notary would gain direct or indirect financial benefit.
feedback: Correct. Screen the underlying interest.
Equipment does not remove a financial stake.
The handbook provides no blanket waiver.
Indirect and later benefits remain within the stated rule.

questions.stem: A bank employee is an Arkansas notary and is asked to notarize an ordinary bank customer's signature. The employee is neither personally involved nor a bank representative in this instrument. Which statement fits?
options: Employment alone always forbids the act
The employer's party status alone does not disqualify the employee
The employee must notarize regardless of circumstances
questions.explanation: The handbook permits corporate employees to act when they are not personally involved or representing the corporation in the instrument.
feedback: The handbook expressly recognizes eligible employee acts.
All identity and other safeguards still apply.
Correct. Check the employee's actual role and interest.
The notary still evaluates the actual request.

questions.stem: An Arkansas corporate officer signs for the corporation and is also asked to notarize the counterparty's signature on that instrument. What controls?
options: The officer's job title alone grants neutrality
The client's agreement removes every conflict
The corporation's seal substitutes for impartiality
The notary is acting as the corporation's representative in the transaction
questions.explanation: The handbook bars corporate-representative or personally involved notaries from notarial acts concerning that instrument.
feedback: The actual representative role creates the problem.
Consent does not remove the stated disqualification.
A corporate seal cannot create impartiality.
Correct. Use another eligible notary.

questions.stem: A company proposes that an Arkansas notary sign its contract as representative but certify only the other party. What is the proper response?
options: Decline the notarial role on that instrument
Proceed because only the other party's signature is notarized
Use a journal instead of a certificate
questions.explanation: The handbook's corporate-representation restriction concerns notarial acts on the instrument.
feedback: Correct. Obtain an independent eligible notary.
Certifying another signature does not remove the notary's transaction role.
A journal does not remove the conflict.
A reduced fee does not change representative status.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary gains an indirect personal stake through the document but receives no immediate cash. How should the interest be screened?
options: Ask only whether the customer pays
Let the notary's employer decide the law
questions.explanation: The handbook includes indirect financial benefit in the conflict rule.
feedback: The rule is broader than same-day cash.
Correct. Assess the actual transaction benefit.
A customer fee is a separate question.
An employer cannot waive the state's conflict standard.

questions.stem: An Arkansas non-attorney advertises as 'notario publico' without any qualification notice. What does the handbook require?
options: Only a larger font for the title
The specified non-attorney/immigration disclaimer in English and Spanish
questions.explanation: The handbook describes the bilingual notice required when using the listed notario terminology.
feedback: Title size alone does not provide the notice.
A telephone number does not state the required limitations.
Correct. Include the required notice.
Price does not satisfy advertising requirements.

questions.stem: An Arkansas 'notario' advertisement includes the required notice only in Spanish. What should be corrected?
options: Provide the notice in both English and Spanish
questions.explanation: The handbook requires the notice in both languages.
feedback: Contact details do not resolve the language omission.
Stamp color is unrelated to advertising.
An endorsement cannot substitute for the notice.
Correct. Both versions are required.

questions.stem: A non-attorney Arkansas notary's notario advertisement implies the notary is a licensed attorney. Which required notice element directly addresses that implication?
options: The statement that the advertiser is not a licensed attorney and cannot practice law
A statement that every document is approved
questions.explanation: The prescribed notice expressly disclaims licensed-attorney status and legal practice.
feedback: Correct. Do not imply a legal qualification the notice disclaims.
Scheduling information does not address professional status.
Notarization does not approve every document.
A slogan is not the required professional-status notice.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notario advertisement states that the notary represents an immigration agency. Which required limitation contradicts that claim?
options: The required notice disclaims agency representation and immigration assistance
A promise of a quick appointment
questions.explanation: The required notice disclaims representation of a government agency with immigration or citizenship authority.
feedback: Office hours do not describe legal authority.
Correct. Follow the notice's agency and assistance limitations.
A commission number does not grant immigration-agency status.
Speed does not establish governmental authority.

questions.stem: A signer asks an Arkansas notary to certify that a transaction happened yesterday although no act occurred then. What is appropriate?
options: Choose the requested date to help the client
Refuse to certify a false act date
Have the client initial the false date
questions.explanation: The notary's certificate must truthfully state the actual date and act.
feedback: Convenience does not permit backdating.
Payment cannot authorize false certification.
Correct. Record the actual event if a lawful act occurs.
Initials do not make an untrue date true.

questions.stem: An Arkansas office keeps sheets with a notary's signature and seal already applied for future customer documents. What is the problem?
options: The notary signed and sealed incomplete certificates before actual acts
questions.explanation: The handbook prohibits placing signature or seal on an incomplete certificate or before the required signing.
feedback: Storage color does not resolve the invalid procedure.
Quantity does not change the rule.
Printer age is unrelated.
Correct. Complete each actual act and certificate.

questions.stem: An Arkansas client says an absent co-signer gave permission to use the co-signer's name in the appearance certificate. What should the notary do?
options: Certify only appearances that actually occurred
Treat private permission as physical appearance
Let the attending signer apply the notary seal
State that both appeared to avoid a delay
questions.explanation: Certificate names represent actual appearance before the notary.
feedback: Correct. An absent person's permission does not create the certified event.
Permission and appearance are different facts.
The signer cannot complete the notary's official act.
Avoiding delay does not justify a false statement.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary knows the certificate's venue is false but the client promises no one will check. What controls?
options: The prohibition on known or believed false certificate information
questions.explanation: A certificate cannot truthfully describe a location the notary knows is false.
feedback: Confidence does not alter the actual venue.
Correct. Use the real act location.
Transaction value does not change venue.
Lack of complaint does not authorize false information.

questions.stem: An Arkansas supervisor instructs a notary to stamp first and check the signer later. Which sequence is required?
options: Follow the supervisor regardless of law
Establish identity and complete the act before final certificate execution
Let the customer choose whether identity matters
questions.explanation: Identity is a pre-act responsibility, and signature/seal finish the completed certificate.
feedback: Employment instructions cannot replace legal duties.
Identity applies regardless of payment.
Correct. Do not reverse the safeguards.
The customer cannot waive the notary's identity responsibility.

questions.stem: An Arkansas client presents a questionable document and the notary is uncomfortable proceeding. Does the official FAQ compel every requested act?
options: Yes, any document must be notarized
Yes, whenever a fee is offered
No, the FAQ says every presented document need not be notarized
questions.explanation: The official FAQ recognizes that a notary is not required to notarize every document presented.
feedback: The FAQ rejects a universal obligation.
A fee does not compel a prohibited or unsuitable act.
The notary makes the official decision.
Correct. Evaluate the actual circumstances.
questions.reference: FAQ, Must I notarize every document?

questions.stem: A customer wants to report a suspected Arkansas notarial violation to the Secretary of State. What complaint form does the handbook describe?
options: A written signed complaint with relevant document evidence
questions.explanation: The handbook describes signed written complaints and inclusion of the questioned document.
feedback: Correct. Use the official complaint procedure.
A rumor does not meet the described signed-written process.
A rating is not the office's complaint filing.
A supplier invoice does not describe the alleged act.

questions.stem: A notary complaint in Arkansas alleges criminal forgery. Which role does the handbook assign to the Secretary of State?
options: The office does not investigate criminal matters like forgery
questions.explanation: The handbook distinguishes administrative complaints from criminal investigations through appropriate legal authorities.
feedback: The handbook does not assign exclusive prosecution.
Correct. Criminal concerns belong with the appropriate legal authorities.
An administrative office does not automatically convict.
The office is not the general police warrant authority.

questions.stem: An Arkansas customer files an administrative notary complaint but omits the questioned notarized document. What would the handbook recommend adding?
options: A copy of the document containing the questioned notarization
Only the complaint writer's business logo
questions.explanation: The handbook asks that the relevant document accompany the written complaint.
feedback: A sales brochure is not evidence of the questioned certificate.
A passport does not ordinarily show the disputed act.
Correct. Provide the actual record supporting the complaint.
A logo does not identify the act.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary says a commission authorizes any legal service a client requests. Which understanding is correct?
options: The commission creates unlimited legal powers
The customer can expand the office by contract
Employer permission creates any public power
The notary may perform the acts authorized by law
questions.explanation: The handbook describes legally defined notarial powers and their limits.
feedback: The office has defined powers.
A private agreement does not create public authority.
An employer cannot enlarge statutory office.
Correct. Identify the authorized act before proceeding.

questions.stem: A courier offers an Arkansas notary a valuable bonus contingent on certifying an appearance that never occurred. What is the proper action?
options: Reject the false certification regardless of the bonus
Accept if the bonus is called travel
Ask the courier to hold the seal
questions.explanation: A benefit cannot authorize false certification or supply a missing appearance.
feedback: Correct. The certificate must reflect the actual lawful act.
Relabeling does not create the event.
A fee entry cannot cure the absent appearance.
Seal custody does not change the truth of the certificate.
questions.reference: pp. 1 and 15–17, Impartiality and false certificates

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary is asked to certify an affidavit without knowing whether the signer is the named affiant. What duty must be resolved?
options: The affiant's identity before the sworn act
questions.explanation: The affidavit procedure includes witnessing the affiant's identity and signature.
feedback: Delivery does not establish identity.
Correct. Establish identity and administer the required oath or affirmation.
Copy price is a separate issue.
Insurance does not identify the participant.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary's certificate includes facts inserted by the customer after the notary signed and sealed it. Which protective practice was missed?
options: Finish the certificate before signing and sealing
questions.explanation: The handbook requires the notary to complete certificate information first to prevent false later insertions.
feedback: Color does not prevent the procedural defect.
A charge does not validate later alterations.
Correct. Control completion of the certificate.
A journal can support evidence and is not the defect.

questions.stem: An Arkansas corporate employee is personally a party to the employer's instrument. Which otherwise permissible rule becomes unavailable?
options: The rule allowing disinterested employees to notarize employer documents
questions.explanation: The employee exception requires no personal involvement or representative role in that instrument.
feedback: Fee authority does not cure the transaction conflict.
Territorial authority does not cure impartiality.
Copy powers do not authorize this signature act.
Correct. Personal involvement defeats the employee condition.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary sees that the document's certificate asserts a fact the notary reasonably believes false, although certainty is incomplete. What wording in the handbook matters?
options: Information known or believed false must not be certified
Only a final court judgment can justify refusing
questions.explanation: The handbook includes information the notary believes false among defective certificate content.
feedback: Correct. Resolve the factual problem before certifying.
A court judgment is not the stated prerequisite.
The notary is responsible for their certificate.
The handbook does not require certifying doubtful false statements.

questions.stem: An Arkansas applicant wants an electronic commission before the traditional commission reaches good standing. What sequence applies?
questions.explanation: Electronic eligibility depends on a traditional commission in good standing.
feedback: Software does not supply ordinary authority.
Correct. Then apply for electronic qualification.
Commissions cannot be borrowed.
Electronic plans do not eliminate ordinary commissioning.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary applicant's filing is accepted. What is the next educational step?
options: Complete the required electronic training and exam
Repeat only the ordinary bond purchase
questions.explanation: The dedicated page places electronic training and examination after application acceptance.
feedback: Correct. Follow the electronic qualification sequence.
A bond does not replace specialized training.
Advertising does not complete qualification.
Another state's exam is not the required assessment.

questions.stem: An Arkansas electronic applicant wants the official training and exam in one account. Who offers the state's linked combined process?
options: The American Society of Notaries on behalf of the Secretary of State
A private customer selected at random
questions.explanation: The state links the ASN combined online course and exam.
feedback: The provider must be the authorized route.
The recorder handles a different commissioning stage.
Correct. Use the link from the official state page.
Customers do not administer this qualification.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary has eight months left on the paper commission and expects a new full ten-year electronic term. What governs expiration?
questions.explanation: The electronic commission runs concurrently with the traditional commission.
feedback: Software purchase does not create a separate ten-year term.
Billing cycles do not set commission expiration.
Calendar-year change does not set this term.
Correct. Consider the short remaining ordinary term.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary's two-year refresher date approaches. What must be completed?
options: A new driver's license regardless of expiry
questions.explanation: Electronic notaries must complete approved refresher training every two years.
feedback: Correct. Track this separately from the ordinary ten-year term.
ID renewal does not replace training.
Business registration is a different obligation.
A survey is not the approved course.

questions.stem: An Arkansas electronic applicant fails both permitted exam attempts within twelve months. What does the rule provide?
options: Unlimited immediate attempts under the same process
Automatic qualification after paying a fee
questions.explanation: The rule limits attempts to two in twelve months and directs repeating the specified process after failure.
feedback: The rule sets an attempt limit.
Correct. Follow §20-103(b) as directed.
A payment does not create a pass.
Renaming the attempt does not evade the rule.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary misses required refresher training. What consequence does the handbook describe?
questions.explanation: The handbook describes suspension of provider access until the training and required amendment are completed.
feedback: Missing training does not renew authority.
A business card cannot cure the omission.
Correct. Complete the stated reinstatement requirements.
The requirement remains applicable.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary has approval for in-person electronic acts using a platform lacking approved RON capability. May a signer remain elsewhere?
options: Yes, with a scanned ID alone
Yes, because the document is electronic
No, the in-person electronic route requires physical proximity
questions.explanation: Remote appearance requires approved RON technology, beyond ordinary in-person electronic tools.
feedback: A phone call does not create approved RON capability.
A scan alone does not satisfy the remote route.
Electronic record format does not remove appearance requirements.
Correct. Use the authorized route matching the technology.
questions.reference: Physical proximity and approved RON technology

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary receives a request through ordinary Zoom. Which platform condition matters?
options: Use an approved RON solution with required safeguards
Any video app is automatically approved
The signer can approve the vendor for the state
questions.explanation: The state excludes ordinary video apps as substitutes for approved RON technology.
feedback: Correct. Check the current approved-provider list.
Video capability alone is insufficient.
Camera price does not establish compliance.
Private consent cannot create state approval.

questions.stem: A RON provider offers video but no identity-proofing or credential-analysis tools. What does Arkansas's official guidance require?
options: Approved technology with identity-proofing and credential-analysis safeguards
questions.explanation: The official RON description includes secure video and identity safeguards.
feedback: Speed alone cannot supply missing identity processes.
Correct. Confirm the approved solution supports the required functions.
A paper seal cannot replace remote identity tools.
A testimonial is not credential analysis.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary acts remotely from an Arkansas office for a signer in another state. What does the location rule permit?
options: The signer may be outside Arkansas while the notary remains in Arkansas
questions.explanation: The state permits an out-of-state principal while requiring the notary's Arkansas location.
feedback: The dedicated page allows a broader signer location.
Residence is not the stated geographic limit.
Correct. Other RON requirements still apply.
The notary must remain within Arkansas.

questions.stem: An Arkansas RON service plans to discard recordings after one year. What retention period does the official page identify for the provider?
questions.explanation: The official RON page requires solution-provider recording retention for five years.
feedback: Thirty days is too short.
One year is too short.
Two years is the refresher interval, not this retention period.
Correct. Confirm the provider's storage arrangement.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary in good standing chooses an already approved RON solution. Does the dedicated page require a separate additional RON registration beyond eNotary qualification?
options: It states no additional registration requirement for that eNotary
A new ordinary commission for every session
questions.explanation: The dedicated page says no additional registration requirements for eNotaries using approved RON technology.
feedback: Correct. The approved technology and other safeguards remain required.
Each session does not create a new ordinary commission.
A marriage license is unrelated.
Another state appointment does not replace Arkansas RON conditions.

questions.stem: An Arkansas electronic document contains a typed signature but no notarial certificate. What is missing?
options: A certificate stating the notarial act performed
questions.explanation: An electronic signature alone is not notarization and the document needs a proper certificate.
feedback: File size does not supply the certificate.
Correct. Complete the actual lawful act.
A receipt does not describe the act.
A password is not certificate wording.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary recognizes the look of a customer's electronic signature and wants to rely on that alone for identity. What does the handbook say?
options: Identity cannot rest merely on familiarity with the electronic signature
questions.explanation: The handbook expressly rejects mere electronic-signature familiarity as an identity basis.
feedback: The handbook identifies this as insufficient.
Billing does not verify the signer.
Correct. Perform the required identity procedure.
A signature does not determine citizenship.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary's ordinary commission is revoked. What happens to electronic authority?
options: It survives until the software subscription ends
It converts to another state's commission
questions.explanation: The electronic commission depends on the traditional commission's good standing.
feedback: A subscription cannot preserve a revoked public office.
Revocation does not transfer authority across states.
Revocation removes authority.
Correct. The provider is notified and access is revoked.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary changes a recorded physical address. Which notification period does the handbook give?
options: Only when the provider sends a bill
questions.explanation: Specified personal-information changes require state notice within thirty days.
feedback: Correct. Follow the appropriate amendment route.
Waiting ten years misses the duty.
Provider billing does not set the reporting deadline.
Customers do not trigger official reporting obligations.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary updates the state record but leaves a solution provider's record inaccurate. What additional step is described?
options: Complete the provider's update requirements too
questions.explanation: The handbook requires following the provider's personal-information update procedures as well as notifying the state.
feedback: The handbook expressly addresses provider updates.
Correct. Keep both relevant records consistent.
Revoking the ordinary record is not the correction method.
Accounts are attributable to the actual notary.

questions.stem: An Arkansas electronic applicant provides only one email address although the electronic process requests primary and secondary contacts. What should be supplied?
options: No way to contact the applicant
questions.explanation: The handbook calls for a primary and secondary email when applying electronically.
feedback: A fax is not both requested emails.
A social account does not fill the stated fields.
Correct. Keep the contacts current.
The process relies on official contact information.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary changes the secondary email used in the electronic application. What does the handbook require?
options: Notify the state within thirty days
questions.explanation: A change to either electronic application email must be reported within thirty days.
feedback: Retirement is too late.
The change concerns the notary's contact.
Coworker notice does not amend the official record.
Correct. Use the appropriate update process.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary allows an assistant to use the notary's electronic signing device while the notary is absent. Which control principle applies?
options: The system must remain accessible only by and attributable to the notary
A manager can acquire authority by password
questions.explanation: The handbook defines sole-control technology as accessible only by the notary and attributable to that individual.
feedback: Correct. Do not delegate the official signing identity.
Employment does not create a shared commission.
A password does not appoint the manager.
A waiver cannot create another person's official authority.

questions.stem: An Arkansas provider says a document is tamper-evident. What does that term mean in the handbook?
options: Changes display evidence of the alteration
questions.explanation: Tamper-evident means electronic changes leave visible evidence of change.
feedback: The term describes detectability, not impossibility of all changes.
Correct. Preserve the required evidence of alteration.
Certificate requirements still apply.
Tamper evidence does not establish substantive truth.

questions.stem: A remote Arkansas signer holds an identification card too far from the camera for analysis. What does remote presentation require?
options: An image of sufficient quality for identification and credential analysis
questions.explanation: The handbook's definition requires a usable identification image.
feedback: Color alone does not establish the credential.
A verbal number does not supply the required image.
Correct. Obtain sufficiently clear presentation.
A subject line cannot support analysis.

questions.stem: An Arkansas RON session plays a recording so the notary cannot interact simultaneously with the signer. Which technology definition is unmet?
questions.explanation: The handbook defines communication technology through simultaneous visual and audio communication.
feedback: Storage does not supply contemporaneous interaction.
Fees do not cure an appearance defect.
Printing is unrelated to simultaneous appearance.
Correct. Use approved real-time communication.

questions.stem: An Arkansas customer asks why credential analysis differs from identity proofing. Which task describes credential analysis?
options: Evaluating the validity of the government-issued identity credential through approved data-based review
questions.explanation: Credential analysis concerns the presented identification credential's validity.
feedback: Correct. Identity proofing addresses the individual's identity through relevant data.
Fairness is outside this identity technology.
Tax assessment is unrelated.
Public commission terms are set by law.

questions.stem: An Arkansas RON service reviews personal information from public and proprietary sources to affirm an individual's identity. Which term fits?
questions.explanation: The handbook identifies that data-based individual-identity process as identity proofing.
feedback: Embossing concerns a physical impression.
Correct. Distinguish it from analyzing the credential itself.
County recording completes commissioning steps.
A corporate oath is a different act.

questions.stem: An Arkansas notary sees an obsolete broad FAQ sentence saying remote acts are unavailable. A dedicated current state RON page describes approved remote acts. Which source treatment is appropriate?
options: Erase the distinction between ordinary and approved remote work
Assume any video app now works
Use the dedicated RON instructions for approved remote acts
questions.explanation: The current dedicated page addresses the approved RON exception to ordinary physical presence.
feedback: The exception has specific qualifications and technology.
Remote permission does not approve arbitrary apps.
Correct. Retain ordinary physical presence outside that route.
Another state's procedure does not govern Arkansas authority.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary buys a provider plan that supports in-person electronic work only. What should be checked before advertising RON?
options: Whether the provider and selected service have approved RON capability
questions.explanation: The state distinguishes in-person electronic providers and approved remote-capable solutions.
feedback: A logo does not identify approved features.
Wallpaper is unrelated.
Demand does not grant approval.
Correct. Match actual approved functionality to the proposed service.

questions.stem: An Arkansas eNotary chooses a mobile device for electronic signing. What does the handbook say about platform compatibility?
options: Provider requirements vary and some support mobile devices
Every provider must support every device
Only one operating system is universally permitted
Buying a tablet automatically grants electronic authority
questions.explanation: The handbook describes varying devices and operating-system support by provider.
feedback: Correct. Check the selected approved provider's requirements.
It expressly notes differences.
No universal operating-system restriction is stated.
Hardware purchase is separate from commissioning.

questions.stem: An Arkansas electronic notary charges nothing for a remote service and assumes this removes the certificate and identity steps. Which conclusion is correct?
options: Free services have no notarial safeguards
The certificate and identity requirements still apply
Only the recording can replace identity
questions.explanation: Charging is optional, while the required notarial procedure remains applicable.
feedback: A waived fee does not waive public duties.
Correct. Perform the complete lawful act.
A recording does not by itself replace identification.
A receipt does not establish the notarial act.

cards.title: Eligibility connection
cards.front: What establishes an ordinary Arkansas resident's state connection?
cards.rule: Arkansas legal residence satisfies the stated connection.
cards.boundary: Adjoining-state and military-spouse routes have separate conditions.
cards.mixup: A mailing address is not automatically a qualifying residence.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 1

cards.title: Minimum age
cards.front: When can a young applicant qualify?
cards.rule: Applicants must be at least eighteen.
cards.boundary: Buying supplies cannot replace the age qualification.
cards.mixup: An employer's permission does not change the minimum.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 1

cards.title: Bond continuity
cards.front: What does the ordinary application require financially?
cards.rule: Obtain a qualifying $7,500 surety bond.
cards.boundary: Renewal requires a new bond.
cards.mixup: A receipt for an old bond is not the new instrument.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, pp. 2 and 6

cards.title: Matching names
cards.front: How should official application names be aligned?
cards.rule: Keep the application, bond and electronic signature consistent.
cards.boundary: Use the current form's exact-name instructions.
cards.mixup: A common nickname may differ from the submitted official name.
cards.source: BCS Notary and Apostille Filing Module User Guide, July 2026, pp. 10–12

cards.title: Two oath stages
cards.front: What remains after an application is approved?
cards.rule: Complete county recording and return the recorded oath to the state.
cards.boundary: The state must process it before activation.
cards.mixup: Approval alone does not complete the office.
cards.source: BCS Notary and Apostille Filing Module User Guide, July 2026, p. 13

cards.title: Oath return method
cards.front: How is the recorded oath returned under the current guide?
cards.rule: Use mail or in-person delivery.
cards.boundary: The July 2026 guide says oath upload is unavailable.
cards.mixup: Electronic application filing does not make every later filing electronic.
cards.source: BCS Notary and Apostille Filing Module User Guide, July 2026, p. 13

cards.title: Reporting changes
cards.front: How soon are name or address changes reported?
cards.rule: File the required amendment within thirty days.
cards.boundary: Name changes require paper and certified evidence.
cards.mixup: A vendor update alone does not amend the state record.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 6

cards.title: Territorial authority
cards.front: Where does the ordinary Arkansas commission operate?
cards.rule: The commission permits acts throughout Arkansas.
cards.boundary: It does not authorize acting physically in another state.
cards.mixup: County of commission does not limit ordinary statewide territory.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 9

cards.title: Satisfactory identity
cards.front: What is the ordinary Arkansas identity standard?
cards.rule: The notary must be certain of the signer's identity.
cards.boundary: Government photo-and-signature ID is recommended.
cards.mixup: Another state's exclusive credential list is not Arkansas's rule.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 9

cards.title: Personal recognition
cards.front: How does personal recognition relate to suggested photo ID?
cards.rule: The handbook recognizes a personally known signer.
cards.boundary: Recognition must establish the actual person's identity.
cards.mixup: Knowing one family member does not identify every relative.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 9

cards.title: Willing participation
cards.front: What should be assessed before the act?
cards.rule: The signer should understand the document and act freely.
cards.boundary: A companion's pressure can require stopping.
cards.mixup: Payment does not establish willingness.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 13

cards.title: Direct communication
cards.front: What language connection does the handbook require?
cards.rule: Signer and notary communicate directly in a language both understand.
cards.boundary: The handbook also addresses understood signature characters.
cards.mixup: A translated office sign does not supply mutual communication.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, pp. 13–14

cards.title: True venue
cards.front: Which location belongs in the certificate venue?
cards.rule: State the actual location of the act.
cards.boundary: That county may differ from commission county.
cards.mixup: A preprinted county does not change the real location.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 14

cards.title: Separate appearances
cards.front: How are signers who attend separately handled?
cards.rule: Use separate certificates accurately describing individual appearances.
cards.boundary: Do not state that absent signers appeared together.
cards.mixup: A joint document does not create a joint appearance.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 17

cards.title: Signing by mark
cards.front: What supports a mark used as a signature?
cards.rule: The mark is made before the notary and at least one disinterested witness.
cards.boundary: Add the prescribed participant notation.
cards.mixup: The one-witness mark route differs from third-party signing.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 13

cards.title: Signature by direction
cards.front: What if a principal cannot sign or mark?
cards.rule: The principal may direct a disinterested third party before two disinterested witnesses and the notary.
cards.boundary: Witness signatures and explanatory wording remain necessary.
cards.mixup: A volunteer cannot supply the principal's direction.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 13

cards.title: Optional register
cards.front: How does Arkansas describe traditional journaling?
cards.rule: The handbook recommends a register for ordinary traditional acts.
cards.boundary: Recommendation should be stated accurately.
cards.mixup: Do not invent a universal paper-journal mandate.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Evidence and recollection
cards.front: Why keep relevant contemporaneous notes?
cards.rule: They help reconstruct past acts and can serve as evidence.
cards.boundary: An entry should describe what actually happened.
cards.mixup: A detailed invented account is not reliable evidence.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Participant details
cards.front: What participant fields are suggested?
cards.rule: Record each notarized person's name, address and signature.
cards.boundary: Identify actual participants.
cards.mixup: The fee payer may differ from the signer.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Act and record
cards.front: What should distinguish one register entry from another?
cards.rule: Include the date, act type and document type.
cards.boundary: Separate relevant factual context into notes.
cards.mixup: A bare word like notarized omits useful detail.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Fee record
cards.front: How should collected charges appear in the recommended register?
cards.rule: Keep an itemized list of fees collected.
cards.boundary: Describe the actual charge or free service.
cards.mixup: A standard advertised price may differ from the amount collected.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Custody at departure
cards.front: What happens to notarial materials when employment ends?
cards.rule: The notary retains the commission's documents and equipment.
cards.boundary: Employer payment does not transfer the public office.
cards.mixup: A departing employee's journal does not become a successor's authority.
cards.source: Secretary of State notary FAQs, Employer and journal FAQ

cards.title: Seal identity
cards.front: Which personal details belong in the official seal?
cards.rule: Include official name, commission number, commission county and expiration.
cards.boundary: Include the required Arkansas and Notary Public wording.
cards.mixup: A company logo cannot replace commission information.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 7

cards.title: Forbidden emblems
cards.front: What state symbols must be excluded from the seal?
cards.rule: Do not include the Arkansas Great Seal or state outline.
cards.boundary: The official notary seal has its own prescribed content.
cards.mixup: Public appointment does not authorize every state emblem.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 7

cards.title: Blue or black
cards.front: Which inks apply to official paper completion?
cards.rule: Use blue or black for the notary signature and seal.
cards.boundary: An embosser must produce a reproducible inked impression.
cards.mixup: A dry raised impression may disappear in copies.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, pp. 7–8

cards.title: Complete certificate
cards.front: What must accompany signature and seal?
cards.rule: A completed certificate stating the actual act, date and venue.
cards.boundary: Complete it before signing and sealing.
cards.mixup: A stamp by itself does not describe a notarization.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, pp. 14–17

cards.title: Reasonable fees
cards.front: What governs a charged Arkansas notarial fee?
cards.rule: The fee must be reasonable, disclosed and agreed in advance.
cards.boundary: A notary may provide a free service.
cards.mixup: Advance agreement alone does not remove reasonableness.
