cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 18

cards.title: Obsolete devices
cards.front: How are replaced or resigned seals handled?
cards.rule: The handbook directs destroying the previous seal.
cards.boundary: Keep current commission information on active equipment.
cards.mixup: A replacement does not create two active identities.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Stolen seal notice
cards.front: What follows discovery of a lost or stolen seal?
cards.rule: Notify the state in writing and follow replacement-number instructions.
cards.boundary: Use the new number on the replacement stamp.
cards.mixup: Buying an identical stamp silently leaves the problem unresolved.
cards.source: Secretary of State notary FAQs, Lost or stolen seal FAQ

cards.title: Commercial facsimile
cards.front: What limits the special facsimile method?
cards.rule: File the required information before use on qualifying commercial documents.
cards.boundary: Deeds and real-estate conveyances are excluded.
cards.mixup: A registered facsimile is not a universal document shortcut.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 8

cards.title: Permissible originals
cards.front: What can ordinary Arkansas copy certification cover?
cards.rule: A permitted record outside the excluded vital/public categories.
cards.boundary: The notary makes or supervises copying.
cards.mixup: A customer's already-made copy alone does not establish the procedure.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Vital records
cards.front: Which examples belong to the vital-record exclusion?
cards.rule: Birth and death certificates are excluded.
cards.boundary: Use the responsible issuing authority's certified-copy process.
cards.mixup: A family's consent does not enlarge the notary's copy power.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Public records
cards.front: Which court-related examples are excluded?
cards.rule: Marriage licenses, divorce decrees and court orders are listed public records.
cards.boundary: A private cover letter does not change an attachment's classification.
cards.mixup: Sensitive information does not make a court record privately issued.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Passport allowance
cards.front: What specific identification-copy examples are permitted?
cards.rule: The handbook permits passport and driver's-license copies.
cards.boundary: Follow the original and supervised-copy procedure.
cards.mixup: A true copy does not become a replacement identity credential.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Faithful reproduction
cards.front: What does a true and perfect copy require?
cards.rule: The reproduction must faithfully match the original presented.
cards.boundary: Missing sides, missing pages and alterations defeat that claim.
cards.mixup: Legible first-page text does not prove the whole copy accurate.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Limited certificate
cards.front: What does the copy certificate actually establish?
cards.rule: It identifies a faithful reproduction of the original.
cards.boundary: It does not adjudicate the original's legal contents.
cards.mixup: A copy certificate is not a contract-enforceability opinion.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Comparison evidence
cards.front: Why may the notary retain a comparison copy?
cards.rule: It can help determine whether the certified document was altered later.
cards.boundary: Retention is described as permitted.
cards.mixup: Keeping evidence does not transfer ownership of the original.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 12

cards.title: Party interest
cards.front: What transaction role disqualifies the notary?
cards.rule: The notary cannot act on a document to which the notary is a party.
cards.boundary: Direct or indirect financial benefit also matters.
cards.mixup: A waived fee does not erase a transaction stake.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 1

cards.title: Corporate boundary
cards.front: When may an employee notarize an employer transaction?
cards.rule: Only when not personally involved or acting as the corporation's representative in the instrument.
cards.boundary: Review the actual role.
cards.mixup: Being an employee alone does not establish either automatic permission or prohibition.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 18

cards.title: Truthful certificates
cards.front: What information must be excluded?
cards.rule: Do not certify information known or believed false.
cards.boundary: Record the act that actually occurred.
cards.mixup: A client's indemnity promise cannot make a false statement true.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 15

cards.title: Notario advertising
cards.front: What notice accompanies the listed notario terminology?
cards.rule: Include the prescribed notice in English and Spanish.
cards.boundary: It disclaims attorney status and immigration-agency representation or assistance.
cards.mixup: A business card's disclaimer must satisfy the applicable advertising requirement.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 17

cards.title: Complaint evidence
cards.front: How does the handbook describe an administrative complaint?
cards.rule: Submit a signed written complaint with the questioned document.
cards.boundary: The official complaint form is the preferred method.
cards.mixup: A review-site rating does not itself file the state complaint.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 18

cards.title: Criminal allegations
cards.front: Who handles alleged forgery or other crimes?
cards.rule: The handbook directs criminal matters to appropriate legal authorities.
cards.boundary: The state notary office's administrative role is separate.
cards.mixup: An administrative complaint does not automatically produce a criminal conviction.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 18

cards.title: Electronic qualification
cards.front: What precedes electronic notarial work?
cards.rule: Hold ordinary good standing, apply electronically, complete required training and exam, and use an approved provider.
cards.boundary: The electronic term ends with the ordinary term.
cards.mixup: Buying software is not appointment.
cards.source: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions, eNotary registration

cards.title: Refresher clock
cards.front: Which continuing education interval applies?
cards.rule: Complete approved electronic refresher training every two years.
cards.boundary: Track it separately from ordinary renewal.
cards.mixup: A ten-year ordinary term does not waive the two-year interval.
cards.source: Code of Arkansas Rules, 21 CAR §20-105, 21 CAR §20-105(c)

cards.title: Remote location
cards.front: Where must the Arkansas remote notary be?
cards.rule: The notary must be physically in Arkansas.
cards.boundary: The signer may be outside Arkansas.
cards.mixup: A mailing address is not physical presence.
cards.source: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions, RON location

cards.title: Approved communication
cards.front: Which technology supports remote appearance?
cards.rule: Use approved RON technology with secure simultaneous audio-video and identity safeguards.
cards.boundary: Ordinary video apps do not supply that approval.
cards.mixup: A clear camera alone is not the complete RON system.
cards.source: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions, Approved technology

cards.title: Recording retention
cards.front: Who retains the remote act recording and for how long?
cards.rule: The solution provider retains it for five years.
cards.boundary: Check the provider's actual storage arrangement.
cards.mixup: The two-year training interval is a different period.
cards.source: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions, Recording retention

cards.title: Identity technologies
cards.front: How do credential analysis and identity proofing differ?
cards.rule: Credential analysis evaluates the ID credential, while identity proofing evaluates the individual through relevant data.
cards.boundary: Electronic-signature familiarity alone is insufficient.
cards.mixup: Recognizing a typed name does not identify a remote person.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, pp. 22–24

cards.title: Sole control
cards.front: Who may use the notary's electronic signature system?
cards.rule: It remains accessible only by and attributable to that notary.
cards.boundary: Administrative help does not transfer the public act.
cards.mixup: Sharing the password does not commission an assistant.
cards.source: Arkansas Notary Public & eNotary Handbook, p. 25

commission.summary: Connect eligibility, application evidence, county recording and state activation before relying on an Arkansas commission.

sections.heading: Eligibility and the filing record
sections.body: Arkansas applicants satisfy the listed age, status, English-literacy and character conditions and review the state's notary law. Residents use their home county for commissioning. The adjoining-state employment/business route and qualifying nonresident military-spouse route require their own connections and address evidence. Keep the official application name consistent with the qualifying bond and signature. The handbook's qualification and application chapters explain these requirements.

sections.heading: Approval through activation
sections.body: The July 2026 BCS guide describes electronic application submission with the bond and exam certificate. Approval produces oath documents for county recording. The recorded oath then goes physically to the state, which must receive and process it before the commission is active. Track status in the official work queue. Renewal requires current evidence and its own completion stages. Name changes use paper with certified documentation, while qualifying address and contact amendments use the current online process.

example.heading: Worked example — opening a second office
example.body: A Benton County resident opens an office in Pulaski County and receives requests in both places. Residence establishes the resident commission county, while statewide authority permits acts in either Arkansas location. For each certificate, the notary uses the actual act county as venue. If the notary later moves residence across county lines, the handbook's transfer and seal-update instructions become relevant.

keyFacts: Ordinary bond amount is $7,500.
County recording and state processing of the recorded oath precede activation.
Commission county and act venue can differ.

identification.summary: Establish the person, willing participation and actual act before completing a certificate that accurately describes the event.

sections.heading: Identity and participation
sections.body: The Arkansas handbook places responsibility for satisfactory identity with the notary. It recommends government-issued identification containing a photograph and signature and recognizes personal recognition. A recommended credential still must identify the actual person presenting it. Before proceeding, check the signer's understanding, free will, understood signature characters and direct communication in a language shared with the notary. Ordinary physical presence remains necessary outside the approved remote route.

sections.heading: Match the procedure and certificate
sections.body: An affidavit requires the affiant's sworn or affirmed statement. A mark procedure requires presence and at least one disinterested witness, while signing by direction for someone unable to sign or mark requires the principal's direction, two disinterested witnesses and the notary, plus the prescribed explanatory completion. Certificates record the true date, venue and participants. Signers attending separately need certificates reflecting their separate appearances. Complete certificate information before applying the official signature and seal.

example.heading: Worked example — accessible signing at a care facility
example.body: A principal understands a document but cannot write or make a mark. The notary first establishes identity, understanding and free will. The principal directs a disinterested third party to sign in the presence of the notary and two disinterested witnesses. Both witnesses sign beside the substituted signature, and the notary adds the prescribed participant explanation and completes the actual notarial certificate.

keyFacts: Identity evidence must satisfy the notary about the actual person.
An affidavit includes an oath or affirmation.
Mark and third-party signature procedures have different witness requirements.

journals.summary: Use an accurate Arkansas register to preserve evidence while describing recommended traditional recordkeeping honestly.

sections.heading: A record that can reconstruct an act
sections.body: The handbook recommends a traditional register or journal and explains its usefulness when the notary must recall a past transaction. It also describes notary records and official papers as admissible in Arkansas courts. Suggested fields include the act date, act type, document type, each notarized person's name, address and signature, relevant notes and itemized fees collected. These entries should preserve actual events rather than an invented account.

sections.heading: Custody and electronic evidence
sections.body: An employer's payment for notarial materials does not transfer the individual's public commission or entitle the employer to keep the notarial materials when the worker leaves. Electronic providers may offer different journaling functions, including automatic entries or optional features. Understand what the selected provider records. A journal entry supplements the performed act and certificate. It cannot create a missing appearance, cure a false certificate or replace the independent RON recording requirement.

example.heading: Worked example — a later signature dispute
example.body: Months after an Arkansas contract signing, a participant disputes which people attended. The notary consults an entry recording the actual two signers, the document type, date, fees and relevant notes about separate appearances. The record can support accurate recollection. It should agree with certificates limited to the appearances the notary actually observed.

keyFacts: The handbook recommends journaling for ordinary traditional acts.
Suggested fields include participant details and itemized fees.
A journal cannot substitute for the underlying required act.

seals-fees.summary: Keep official equipment accurate and distinguish complete certificates, reasonable service fees and the limited commercial facsimile route.

sections.heading: Official seal and signature
sections.body: The Arkansas seal identifies the notary's official name, commission county, commission number and expiration and includes the required office and state wording. It excludes the state outline and Great Seal. Use blue or black ink for the official signature and seal and ensure a legible reproducible impression. A dry embosser needs the prescribed inking. The signature must match the official signature on file, and the seal belongs under or near it on the completed certificate.

sections.heading: Fees and replacement controls
sections.body: A notary may provide free services. A charged fee must be reasonable, disclosed and agreed before the act. Apply Arkansas's rule to the actual service instead of importing another state's fixed amount. Report lost or stolen seals to the state in writing and follow replacement-number instructions. Destroy obsolete seals after replacement or resignation as the handbook directs. The registered commercial facsimile route has filing and ink conditions and excludes real-estate conveyance documents.

example.heading: Worked example — preparing an office fee policy
example.body: An Arkansas office adopts a service schedule. The notary explains the proposed charge before the act, confirms agreement and ensures reasonableness. The notary records the actual charge in the recommended register and completes the certificate using the current official signature and accurate seal. A client receiving a free service still receives the same legally required notarial procedure.

keyFacts: The seal must reproduce clearly in blue or black.
Signature and stamp accompany a completed certificate.
Charged fees must be reasonable and agreed beforehand.

copy-certification.summary: Classify the original and perform the required copying procedure before making a limited true-copy certification.

sections.heading: Classify the document first
sections.body: The Arkansas handbook permits certification of copies of qualifying originals while excluding vital records, public records and specified government-issued documents. Birth and death certificates are vital-record examples. Marriage licenses, divorce decrees and court orders are public-record examples. A private cover letter does not change an attached court record's status. The handbook expressly permits passport and driver's-license copies, which should be read as the stated specific allowances.

sections.heading: Faithful copy and truthful certificate
sections.body: The notary makes or supervises photocopying the original presented and confirms a true and perfect reproduction. Check all relevant pages and sides and resolve missing, blurred or altered material. The sample certificate identifies the source document and actual date and includes the notary's official completion components. The notary may retain a comparison copy to help determine later alteration. This certificate concerns reproduction and does not adjudicate the original transaction's legal effect.

example.heading: Worked example — a mixed submission packet
example.body: A customer brings a private authorization, a driver's license and an attached divorce decree. The notary screens each source separately. The private authorization and driver's-license copy requests can be evaluated under the permitted copying procedure. The decree remains an excluded public record, so the customer needs its official-copy route. One envelope does not make all the records equally eligible.

keyFacts: Vital and public records have stated exclusions.
The notary makes or supervises copying.
Copy fidelity differs from substantive legal validity.

prohibited-acts.summary: Screen transaction interests, corporate roles, certificate truth and advertising statements before accepting an Arkansas notarial request.

sections.heading: Personal interests and corporate work
sections.body: The handbook prohibits notarizing the notary's own signature, a document to which the notary is a party or a document producing direct or indirect financial benefit. Corporate employment alone does not settle the issue. An employee may act on an employer document only when the employee is not personally involved or acting as a representative in that instrument. Review the actual transaction role before assuming an office routine is permissible.

sections.heading: Public statements and complaints
sections.body: Do not sign or seal incomplete certificates or certify information known or believed false. Private consent, prepayment and employer instructions cannot supply an event that never occurred. Advertising with the listed notario terminology requires the prescribed English-and-Spanish notice about attorney status and immigration-related limits. For administrative concerns, the handbook describes a signed written complaint with the questioned document. It separately directs criminal allegations such as forgery to appropriate legal authorities.

example.heading: Worked example — a bank reorganization
example.body: A bank employee regularly notarizes unrelated customer documents. During a reorganization, the employee is designated to sign an instrument as the bank's representative. That new role changes the conflict analysis for the instrument. The employee should arrange another eligible notary for its notarial acts, even though routine employment previously permitted other work.

keyFacts: A party or financial stake can disqualify the notary.
Corporate representation matters independently of ordinary employment.
The notary's certificate must describe true completed events.

electronic-ron.summary: Distinguish electronic qualification, in-person electronic work and approved remote sessions while maintaining current training and controlled technology.

sections.heading: Qualification and continuing conditions
sections.body: An Arkansas electronic applicant first holds traditional good standing, submits the electronic application, completes the required electronic training and exam and selects an approved solution. The electronic term ends with the traditional commission. Approved refresher training recurs every two years under 21 CAR §20-105. Track changes in state and provider records, including required contact details. Revocation of the traditional commission also removes the dependent electronic authority.

sections.heading: The remote session
sections.body: In-person electronic notarization retains physical proximity unless the approved RON route is used. During RON, the notary remains physically in Arkansas, and the signer may be outside the state. Use approved secure simultaneous communication, identity proofing and credential analysis. The provider retains the recording for five years under the dedicated state page. An electronic signature alone is insufficient, and the proper certificate and identity procedure remain necessary. Keep the notary's signing system under sole control.

example.heading: Worked example — choosing a technology service
example.body: An eNotary compares an in-person-only product with an approved RON service. The intended customers will attend remotely, so a signature pad alone cannot supply the needed capability. The notary checks the approved remote service's identity tools, live communication and recording retention, completes the qualification conditions and conducts the session from Arkansas.

keyFacts: Electronic authority depends on ordinary good standing.
The electronic refresher interval is two years.
Approved RON requires the notary's Arkansas physical location.

articles.intent: Understand commission county and mobile-act venue
articles.title: County information in Arkansas mobile notarizations
articles.description: Apply the separate rules for commission county, certificate venue and statewide Arkansas authority.
articles.h1: County information in Arkansas mobile notarizations
articles.lede: A Rogers-based notary meets a customer in an Arkansas hospital outside the commission county. The location changes the certificate's venue while the commission record retains its own county information.

sections.heading: Identify the two county functions
sections.body: The Arkansas handbook places an Arkansas resident's commission in the county of residence and identifies that county on the official seal. The venue in a particular certificate records where the notarial act actually occurred. These entries answer different factual questions. Check each against the correct source before assuming that different county names show a defect.

sections.heading: Use statewide authority accurately
sections.body: The handbook describes jurisdiction throughout Arkansas during the commission term. A customer appointment elsewhere in the state does not ordinarily require a new county commission. Physical travel across the state boundary changes that conclusion. The Arkansas commission does not authorize using its seal for an act the notary performs in a neighboring state.

sections.heading: Separate a visit from a move
sections.body: An occasional hospital visit differs from moving the notary's residence into another Arkansas county. The handbook describes commission transfer and a new seal reflecting the new county after that residence change. A nonresident commissioned through Arkansas employment also follows the relevant employment-county transfer instructions when the qualifying Arkansas job location changes.

sections.heading: Work the hospital example through
sections.body: At the hospital appointment, establish the signer's identity and participation, perform the required act, and enter the hospital county in the venue. The current seal retains the accurate commission county. Relevant notes in a recommended register can record the actual location. If the notary later relocates residence, handle that separate record-and-equipment update.

faqs.q: Must seal county and certificate venue always match?
faqs.a: They can differ when the act occurs outside the commission county but within Arkansas.

faqs.q: Does statewide authority allow an Arkansas act in Missouri?
faqs.a: The handbook does not authorize acts physically performed outside Arkansas under the Arkansas commission.

articles.intent: Distinguish mark and directed third-party signature procedures
articles.title: Accessible signatures in Arkansas notarial work
articles.description: Distinguish a signer's mark from a signature made by a directed third party.
articles.h1: Accessible signatures in Arkansas notarial work
articles.lede: At an Arkansas rehabilitation center, one customer can make a mark and another cannot make any mark. The handbook supplies different procedures for these two situations.

sections.heading: Begin with the person's participation
sections.body: Physical difficulty writing does not by itself answer whether the person understands the document or wishes to sign. The handbook's pre-act checks include identity, understanding, free will and direct communication in a shared language. Establish those facts before selecting a writing accommodation. A companion's eagerness cannot supply the principal's decision.

sections.heading: Use the mark procedure when it fits
sections.body: For a mark, the handbook requires making it in the notary's presence with at least one disinterested witness. The notary adds explanatory wording identifying the signer by mark and the witness or witnesses. This records who made the mark and who observed it. The mark should not be treated as an excuse to omit identity or certificate completion.

sections.heading: Use direction when no mark is possible
sections.body: When the principal cannot sign or make a mark, a disinterested third party may sign at the principal's direction. The principal, two disinterested witnesses and the notary participate as prescribed. Each witness signs beside the substituted signature, and the notary adds the required participant explanation. The third party's independent willingness is insufficient without the principal's direction.

sections.heading: Document the actual procedure
sections.body: The rehabilitation appointments should produce certificates reflecting the act actually performed. Optional register notes can identify the accommodation and participants for later recollection. Do not reuse the one-witness mark arrangement for the more demanding third-party signature procedure. The differences in who signs and how many witnesses attend determine which steps must be completed.

faqs.q: How many witnesses does the handbook require for a mark?
faqs.a: At least one disinterested witness, with the mark made before the notary.

faqs.q: Can a helper sign without the principal's direction?
faqs.a: The described third-party procedure requires the principal's direction and the prescribed presence and witness steps.

articles.intent: Complete accurate certificates when signers attend separately
articles.title: Separate appearances on one Arkansas document
articles.description: Keep certificate names, dates and appearance statements accurate when a document has several signers.
articles.h1: Separate appearances on one Arkansas document
articles.lede: Three siblings are signing an Arkansas property-related packet, but their appointments fall on different days. A single shared document does not establish a shared appearance.

sections.heading: Read what the certificate asserts
sections.body: The handbook explains that including a signer's name in the certificate represents that person's appearance before the notary. Review named participants before signing and sealing. A preprinted list may include people who have not attended. The notary's certificate must follow the actual event and cannot simply reproduce every name appearing elsewhere in the packet.

sections.heading: Use separate certificates for separate attendance
sections.body: When signers cannot appear before the same notary at the same time, the handbook directs separate acknowledgment certificates for the individual signatures. This allows each officer to describe the appearance actually witnessed. Identify the correct person and actual act date for each certificate. A sibling's consent cannot substitute for another sibling's required participation.

sections.heading: Complete the certificate before final execution
sections.body: The notary completes certificate information before applying the official signature and seal. This protects against later insertion of false material. Check the actual venue and date as well as participant names. Signature and stamp are the finishing components of a completed certificate, and a form with blanks should not leave the notary for a customer to finish.

sections.heading: Reconstruct the packet accurately
sections.body: For the siblings' appointments, maintain a clear association between each individual's signature and its certificate. A recommended register can distinguish the dates, act types and relevant attendance notes. The record should support a later explanation of the separate events. It cannot cure a certificate that falsely states everyone attended together on the first appointment date.

faqs.q: Can one attending signer vouch for absent co-signers?
faqs.a: That does not create the absent persons' appearance for the notary's certificate.

faqs.q: Should the certificate use the packet's drafting date?
faqs.a: It must accurately state the actual notarial-act date.

articles.intent: Apply satisfactory identification without importing other-state credential lists
articles.title: Identity decisions for Arkansas paper notarizations
articles.description: Use Arkansas's satisfactory-identity standard and the handbook's recommended evidence.
articles.h1: Identity decisions for Arkansas paper notarizations
articles.lede: An Arkansas service desk receives a familiar customer, a stranger with a government card, and a visitor with only a business membership card. Each requires a decision about the actual person's identity.

sections.heading: Apply the Arkansas standard
sections.body: The handbook assigns responsibility for satisfactory identity to the notary. It recommends government-issued identification containing the signer's photograph and signature and recognizes personal recognition. It does not provide an exclusive ordinary-act credential list. A training list taken from another state should not silently become an Arkansas legal mandate.

sections.heading: Examine the person and evidence together
sections.body: A government card remains evidence to evaluate. If the photograph appears inconsistent with the person presenting it, the card's governmental origin does not resolve the discrepancy. A membership card also does not automatically establish identity. The notary should obtain satisfactory evidence before acting, rather than allowing a deadline or payment to end the inquiry.

sections.heading: Keep other participation checks visible
sections.body: Identity is one checkpoint. The handbook also directs attention to understanding, free will, signature characters and direct communication in a language both participants understand. A genuine identity card does not show that a companion is allowing the signer to choose freely. Ask and observe enough to determine whether the stated procedure can properly proceed.

sections.heading: Use the desk appointments differently
sections.body: The familiar customer's personal recognition may establish identity if the notary is genuinely certain. The stranger's card should be assessed against the actual presenter. The membership-card visitor may require better evidence before the notary is satisfied. In all three cases, complete the actual authorized act and certificate only after the relevant preconditions are met.

faqs.q: Is an expensive or newly printed card conclusive?
faqs.a: The evidence must satisfactorily identify the actual person. Appearance and discrepancies still matter.

faqs.q: Does knowing a signer remove the oath for an affidavit?
faqs.a: An affidavit remains a sworn or affirmed statement. Identity and the required act are separate matters.

articles.intent: Assess employee and representative roles in employer documents
articles.title: Corporate roles and impartial Arkansas notarizations
articles.description: Apply the handbook's distinction between ordinary employment and involvement in the instrument.
articles.h1: Corporate roles and impartial Arkansas notarizations
articles.lede: An Arkansas operations employee notarizes customer documents, then receives authority to sign a major contract for the company. The new transaction role changes the impartiality analysis.

sections.heading: Look beyond who pays for the office
sections.body: The handbook says an employer may pay for the commission, bond and supplies, but the commission remains with the individual. Employer payment neither revokes nor transfers the public office. A manager's instruction therefore does not answer whether a particular notarization is lawful. The notary must evaluate the actual signature and transaction.

sections.heading: Screen direct participation and benefit
sections.body: The notary cannot notarize their own signature, a document to which they are a party or a document yielding direct or indirect financial benefit. Consider the instrument's actual effect on the notary. Renaming a benefit or waiving the ordinary service fee does not remove the underlying transaction stake identified by the handbook.

sections.heading: Apply the corporate-employee boundary
sections.body: An employee may notarize a document to which the employer is a party when the employee is not personally involved or acting as a corporate representative in the instrument. That condition differs from a blanket rule about all bank or company employees. A representative who signs the instrument cannot assume that certifying only the counterparty eliminates the conflict.

sections.heading: Change the workflow when the role changes
sections.body: For the operations employee's major contract, arrange an eligible independent notary once the employee becomes the company's representative in that instrument. For unrelated routine transactions, assess the relevant conditions afresh. Keep any certificate truthful and complete. The employer's commercial deadline cannot supply impartiality or authorize a certificate describing events that never occurred.

faqs.q: Does ordinary employment always prohibit employer-document notarization?
faqs.a: The handbook permits it when the employee is not personally involved or representing the corporation in that instrument.

faqs.q: Can an employer revoke an employee's commission?
faqs.a: The handbook states that the employer cannot revoke the individual's commission.

articles.intent: Classify mixed originals before certifying copies
articles.title: Screen a mixed Arkansas copy-certification packet
articles.description: Distinguish private originals, vital records, public records and the handbook's identification-copy allowances.
articles.h1: Screen a mixed Arkansas copy-certification packet
articles.lede: A customer brings a private authorization, a passport and a court decree to an Arkansas office. The request is one packet, but each original has its own copy-certification classification.

sections.heading: Classify each source separately
sections.body: The handbook permits true-copy certification for eligible documents while excluding vital and public records and specified government-issued records. It lists birth and death certificates as vital records and marriage licenses, divorce decrees and court orders as public records. A private envelope or cover letter does not change an attached decree's source category.

sections.heading: Recognize the specific allowances
sections.body: The same chapter expressly permits passport and driver's-license copies. Apply these specific examples without expanding them into permission for every document issued by government or immigration authorities. The notary should identify exactly what original is being copied. A certified reproduction of an identity credential does not become a replacement credential or establish travel or immigration rights.

sections.heading: Control the reproduction procedure
sections.body: For an eligible original, the notary makes or supervises photocopying. Confirm every relevant page and side and address blurred text or alterations before stating that the copy is true and perfect. The sample certificate records the presented original and actual date and bears the notary's official completion components. An emailed customer-made copy alone omits the required source procedure.

sections.heading: Keep the certification within its scope
sections.body: In the mixed packet, evaluate the private authorization and passport under the permitted route and direct the decree to its responsible official-copy authority. The notary may retain a comparison copy to help check later alteration. The certification concerns faithful reproduction and does not determine whether the original authorization is enforceable or its statements are factually correct.

faqs.q: Can private cover wording make a court order eligible?
faqs.a: The order remains an excluded public-record category under the handbook.

faqs.q: Who must make the copy?
faqs.a: The notary makes or supervises the photocopying of the original presented.

articles.intent: Apply reasonableness, disclosure and agreement in service pricing
articles.title: Agree on Arkansas notarial fees before the act
articles.description: Build a fee conversation around the actual Arkansas rule for ordinary and electronic services.
articles.h1: Agree on Arkansas notarial fees before the act
articles.lede: A mobile Arkansas notary publishes service prices and also volunteers at a community event. Paid and free appointments both require complete notarial procedures.

sections.heading: Begin with the state-specific standard
sections.body: The handbook says Arkansas notaries need not charge. If a charge is made, it must be reasonable, disclosed and agreed before the notarial act. These are cumulative conditions. A fixed amount borrowed from a neighboring state's handbook does not establish the Arkansas rule. Review the actual service and the applicable Arkansas guidance when setting the charge.

sections.heading: Have the discussion before execution
sections.body: Explain the proposed amount while the customer can decide whether to accept the charged service. Revealing the price only after signing and sealing misses the stated sequence. If there is no agreement, resolve the issue before proceeding with a charged act. A posted policy should support a clear conversation about this customer's actual request.

sections.heading: Treat electronic services with the same attention
sections.body: The handbook's electronic chapter also requires a reasonable amount agreed before the act when an electronic fee is charged. Provider subscription costs and available technology do not themselves establish the customer agreement. Explain the actual proposed service accurately. Do not imply that buying an electronic platform removes the ordinary notary's duties toward the signer.

sections.heading: Record what actually happened
sections.body: The suggested Arkansas register includes an itemized list of fees collected. Record the real paid or free service rather than a fictional standard price. At the community event, a waived fee does not remove appearance, identity, oath when required or certificate completion. A no-fee appointment should receive the same care in performing the authorized act.

faqs.q: Must an Arkansas notary always charge?
faqs.a: The handbook permits a notary to provide services without charging.

faqs.q: Does client agreement alone establish a lawful amount?
faqs.a: The handbook also requires reasonableness and prior disclosure.

articles.intent: Use a recommended register for reconstruction and protect correct custody
articles.title: Records that help explain an Arkansas notarial act
articles.description: Use the handbook's register fields to preserve real participants, acts and charges.
articles.h1: Records that help explain an Arkansas notarial act
articles.lede: After leaving an Arkansas employer, a notary receives a question about a past transaction. Accurate personal notarial records can help reconstruct what actually happened.

sections.heading: Describe the recommendation precisely
sections.body: The handbook recommends a register for ordinary traditional acts and explains that it can help when the notary is called to testify. It also states that notary records and official papers are admissible in Arkansas courts. Describe this benefit without inventing a universal mandatory paper-journal rule or endorsing a required commercial brand.

sections.heading: Capture distinct factual fields
sections.body: Suggested fields include act date and type, document type, each notarized person's name, address and signature, a notes section and itemized fees collected. Use these fields to distinguish participants and appointments. A bare word such as notarized offers little help when several documents or separate appearances were involved. Relevant accurate notes preserve the particular procedure.

sections.heading: Keep records consistent with certificates
sections.body: If the act involved a directed third-party signature or signers attending separately, record the actual participants and sequence. The entry should support a certificate limited to true events. An invented ID check or fee entry undermines the record's purpose. Detailed notes cannot create an appearance that never occurred or legalize a knowingly false certificate.

sections.heading: Preserve the individual's responsibility
sections.body: The handbook and FAQ explain that employer-paid notarial materials remain connected to the individual notary. An employer cannot revoke the commission or take over its official use merely because payroll funded it. When employment ends, retain the notarial materials appropriately. A replacement employee needs their own authority and cannot inherit the departed notary's office through the old journal.

faqs.q: Does a journal replace the certificate?
faqs.a: The required act and completed certificate remain necessary. The journal preserves supporting details.

faqs.q: May an employer take over the commission after termination?
faqs.a: The handbook states that the commission belongs to the individual and the employer cannot revoke it.

articles.intent: Understand remote identity tools and control of electronic signatures
articles.title: Identity and sole control in Arkansas electronic notarization
articles.description: Distinguish electronic signatures, credential analysis, identity proofing and a notary's controlled signing system.
articles.h1: Identity and sole control in Arkansas electronic notarization
articles.lede: An Arkansas eNotary recognizes a repeat customer's typed signature and an assistant offers to finish the digital certificate. Familiarity and convenience leave separate identity and control questions.

sections.heading: A signature image is only one component
sections.body: The handbook says adding an electronic signature alone does not perform a notarization. A certificate must describe the notarial act, and the signer's identity must still be verified. Familiarity with the appearance of the customer's electronic signature is expressly insufficient by itself. Evaluate the real participant through the appropriate authorized method.

sections.heading: Separate credential and individual checks
sections.body: The handbook defines credential analysis as approved data-based evaluation of a government-issued identification credential. Identity proofing addresses the individual's identity through personal information from public and proprietary sources. These terms identify different parts of the remote system. A readable card presentation supports the process, while a distant blurred image may be inadequate for identification and analysis.

sections.heading: Keep official signing control individual
sections.body: The sole-control definition requires the notary's signing and sealing system to be accessible only by and attributable to that notary. An assistant's administrative role does not confer public authority. Sharing access so an assistant can apply the official identity while the notary is absent defeats that control. The notary must personally perform the authorized official act.

sections.heading: Connect integrity and accurate completion
sections.body: The handbook defines tamper-evident records through detectable changes. Preserve that electronic integrity while completing a truthful certificate and required identity procedure. In the repeat-customer appointment, recognition of a typed signature cannot replace the actual safeguards, and the assistant cannot complete the public act under a shared credential. The digital format retains the notary's individual responsibility.

sources.title: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions

faqs.q: Are identity proofing and credential analysis identical?
faqs.a: The handbook distinguishes checking the individual from evaluating the identity credential.

faqs.q: May an assistant use the notary's electronic signature account?
faqs.a: The handbook's sole-control principle makes access and attribution specific to the individual notary.

articles.intent: Evaluate remote capability, location, training and recording retention
articles.title: Choose an Arkansas RON service that fits the act
articles.description: Check actual approved remote capability and maintain the separate training and recording conditions.
articles.h1: Choose an Arkansas RON service that fits the act
articles.lede: An Arkansas eNotary compares a signature-pad product with a remote platform. Both use electronic documents, but only the approved RON route permits the signer to attend remotely.

sections.heading: Choose the authorized appearance route
sections.body: The dedicated state page distinguishes in-person electronic notarization from approved remote online notarization. An in-person-only electronic solution retains physical proximity. The RON exception requires an approved provider with secure communication, identity-proofing and credential-analysis safeguards. Ordinary Zoom or FaceTime is not the substitute described by the Secretary of State.

sections.heading: Locate the notary before connecting
sections.body: During the Arkansas RON act, the notary must be physically in Arkansas. The principal may be outside the state under the dedicated guidance. A traveling notary cannot replace this condition with an Arkansas postal address or an active subscription. Confirm the actual location before representing that the session is being performed under Arkansas remote authority.

sections.heading: Track education independently
sections.body: Electronic qualification requires the specific application, training and examination steps after ordinary good standing. Under 21 CAR §20-105, approved refresher training recurs every two years. The handbook describes provider suspension when required refresher training is missed. The ordinary commission's ten-year term and the provider's billing anniversary do not reset that continuing education clock.

sections.heading: Plan the recording and continuing records
sections.body: The dedicated RON page identifies five-year recording retention by the solution provider. Confirm the actual approved service supports that arrangement and simultaneous communication. Keep required state and provider information current. If ordinary authority is revoked, dependent electronic authority also ends. A provider plan, recording archive or customer request cannot preserve a public commission that is no longer valid.

sources.title: Secretary of State eNotary and RON instructions

faqs.q: Can an in-person electronic platform automatically provide RON?
faqs.a: Confirm that the provider and selected service have approved remote capability and the required safeguards.

faqs.q: How long does the state page say the provider retains a RON recording?
faqs.a: Five years. The electronic refresher-training interval is separately two years.
